title: Lowering the enabled-scout cap pauses nothing; tests patch the constant in team_limits
answers: What happens to running scouts when the max enabled scouts is lowered?
How do I patch MAX_ENABLED_SCOUTS_PER_TEAM in tests?
body:
Semantics: a lowered cap only blocks the next ordinary enable (`views._reject_if_enabled_cap_reached`, error names count and cap); disabling/tuning existing scouts stays allowed and raising the cap resumes nothing. Operational scouts still count toward the cap but are exempt from it at seeding.
Tests: the constant is now imported into `team_limits.py`, so patch `products.signals.backend.scout_harness.team_limits.MAX_ENABLED_SCOUTS_PER_TEAM`, not `config_registry`/`views`.
`tools/runs.py` `MAX_SCOUTS_PER_RUNS_QUERY` deliberately stays 10x the constant, not per-project.
Import `team_limits` lazily inside models.py (PLC0415) to keep the django.setup() path light.
applies: tests and behavior around enabled-scout cap in products/signals
says: Running scouts pause when I lower the max enabled scouts limit
How should I adjust the maximum scouts cap for a team in tests
New scout enables fail but existing scouts stay tunable after lowering
Scouts still count against limit but ignore it during seeding
Why doesn't reducing the cap pause any currently running scouts
search: Lowering the enabled-scout cap in products/signals only blocks new scout enables via views._reject_if_enabled_cap_reached; it does not pause existing scouts or resume anything when raised. Tests must patch products.signals.backend.scout_harness.team_limits.MAX_ENABLED_SCOUTS_PER_TEAM, not config_registry or views. The MAX_SCOUTS_PER_RUNS_QUERY constant in tools/runs.py deliberately stays 10x the team cap and is not per-project.
